title: Number & Alphabet Series
intro: A series question shows a sequence built on a hidden rule and asks for the next term, a missing term, or the wrong term. The skill is testing the gaps systematically: first differences, then second differences, then ratios, then patterns on alternate terms. SSC favours arithmetic steps, multiplication chains, squares/cubes, and prime sequences. Write the differences under the numbers — most series confess immediately.

topics.name: Number Series
topics.details: Take first differences between consecutive terms. If they are constant it is an AP; if they grow steadily look at second differences; if terms multiply, find the ratio. Squares, cubes, and 'square ±1' patterns are SSC staples; for longer series test alternate terms.

topics.name: Alphabet Series
topics.details: Convert letters to positions (A=1 … Z=26) and treat it like a number series. The usual rules are a fixed step (+2, +3), a growing step, or skipping a fixed number of letters. Recount positions if a pattern seems to break.

solved.solution: Steps +2, +3, +4 → next +5. K(11) → P(16). Answer P.

topics.name: Alphanumeric & Mixed Series
topics.details: Mixed series interleave letters and numbers (A1, C3, E5 …) or run two patterns at once. Separate the streams: read all the letters as one series and all the numbers as another, solve each, then recombine.

topics.name: Missing & Wrong Term
topics.details: To find a missing term, establish the rule from the surrounding terms and fill the gap. To find the wrong term, compute what each term should be from the rule and flag the one that doesn't fit. Re-derive the rule from at least three clean terms first.

shortcuts: Write first differences under the terms; constant = AP, growing = check 2nd differences.
If terms grow fast, test a constant ratio (GP).
For letters, convert to A=1…Z=26 and treat as numbers.
For mixed series, split letters and numbers into two streams.
Memorise squares to 20 and cubes to 12 — they appear constantly.
mistakes: Miscounting alphabet positions (recount when a pattern "breaks").
Judging the wrong term from only two clean terms.
Missing an alternating two-series pattern in longer sequences.
Confusing +k (AP) with ×k (GP) when numbers are small.
pyq: SSC asks next-term and wrong-term items every Tier; Tier 2 adds alternating and square/cube-based series. Differences-first is the fastest reliable method.

flashcards.q: First check on a number series?

summary: Solve series by testing differences, then ratios, then squares/cubes, then alternating patterns. Convert letters to positions and split mixed series into separate streams. Derive the rule from several clean terms before naming a missing or wrong term.
